title: Low capital requirements for futures trading
claim: Day trading futures requires significantly less capital than stocks; traders can start with as low as $5,000 depending on platform
support: Cited as advantage of futures vs stock trading
mechanism: Futures leverage allows control of large positions with smaller capital
validation: Check current minimums with brokers

title: No short-selling restrictions in futures
claim: Futures trading allows unrestricted short positions without stock borrow requirements
support: Compared as advantage over stock trading
mechanism: Futures are symmetric instruments; shorting is not restricted by uptick rules or borrow availability
validation: Check current rules; note Reg SHO and equity restrictions differ

title: Minimum account for day trading
claim: US day trading has $1,000 minimum but most providers recommend $8,000-10,000; trading with minimum is not worthwhile
support: Platform recommendations and trader practices cited
mechanism: PDT rule requires $2,000+ but realistic trading needs higher cushion to avoid forced liquidations
validation: Confirm current PDT rule and broker enforcement

title: Broker selection and specialization
claim: Broker choice reflects reliability and reputation; experts in one field (e.g., stocks) may be poor in another (e.g., Forex)
support: General principle stated for broker selection
mechanism: Different brokers specialize in different instruments and have varying infrastructure, spreads, and support
failure_modes: Broker quality not correlated with specialization
Single broker offers equal service across assets
validation: Audit broker execution statistics and uptime

title: Futures leverage creates high profit and loss potential
claim: Futures offer high leverage that creates both high-profit potential and significant loss risk; small price changes yield exponentially significant returns
support: Leverage effects explained as core risk/reward
mechanism: Leverage multiplies both gains and losses; borrowing to trade amplifies volatility exposure
validation: Backtest leverage impact on drawdown and recovery

title: Forex market accessible 24/5 with high liquidity
claim: Forex market operates 24 hours/day, 5 days/week with high liquidity, allowing traders to trade at any time
support: Cited as major advantage of forex vs stock trading
mechanism: Global market with overlapping sessions across time zones
validation: Check market hours against broker data

title: Currency pairs and pip concept
claim: Forex pairs quoted as ratios (e.g., EUR/USD); pip is smallest price unit; understanding PIPS essential for position sizing
support: Foundational forex concept
mechanism: Forex quotes show exchange rate; pip is 4th decimal place for most pairs
validation: Check broker pip definitions for accuracy

title: Fundamental and technical analysis in forex
claim: Forex traders use both fundamental analysis (economic data, central bank actions) and technical analysis (patterns, indicators)
support: Both methods presented as valid
mechanism: Fundamentals drive long-term trends; technicals predict short-term moves
failure_modes: Analysis methods fail in volatile periods
validation: Backtest technical and fundamental signals; measure correlation

title: Scalping strategy with small pip targets
claim: Scalping is high-frequency strategy; traders open/close positions for small pip gains (5-10 pips) with tight stop losses
support: Strategy described with typical pip targets
mechanism: High-frequency entries/exits with defined risk; accumulate gains from many small wins
assumptions: Spreads low enough to be profitable
validation: Backtest scalping with full transaction costs; compare to realistic live fills

title: Trading psychology and emotional control
claim: Fear and greed drive poor trading decisions; winning traders control emotions through discipline and routine
support: Psychology presented as critical factor in trader success
mechanism: Emotional decisions override plan; discipline enforces plan adherence
validation: Compare planned vs actual trades; measure deviation frequency

title: Trading plan essential before live trading
claim: Successful traders develop written trading plans with risk limits, position sizing, and entry/exit criteria before trading live
support: Plan and risk management presented as requirements
mechanism: Written plan provides discipline; risk limits prevent catastrophic losses
validation: Check for documented plan; measure adherence via trade logs

title: Options are derivatives with expiration
claim: Options are contracts giving right to buy/sell at specific price by expiration date; value depends on underlying security
support: Definition of options contract
mechanism: Options derive value from underlying; time decay accelerates near expiration
validation: Check contract specifications with exchanges

title: Puts and calls main option types
claim: Calls give right to buy; puts give right to sell. Call buyers profit from price increases; put buyers profit from decreases
support: Foundational options concept
mechanism: Call = long upside; put = long downside; intrinsic value = max(underlying - strike) for calls
validation: Confirm call/put mechanics with exchange documentation

title: Collar strategy limits both upside and downside
claim: Collar = buy protective put + sell covered call; limits gains and losses; used to hedge portfolios at cost
support: Strategy defined with risk/reward profile
mechanism: Put protects downside; call premium offsets put cost; creates defined risk/reward band
validation: Backtest collar effectiveness vs unhedged portfolio

title: Binary options fixed payoff structure
claim: Binary options pay fixed amount if underlying ends above strike, zero otherwise; all-or-nothing payoff
support: Binary options definition and mechanics
mechanism: Fixed payout creates different risk/reward than vanilla options
validation: Verify legality in trader's jurisdiction; check broker licensing

title: Time decay accelerates near options expiration
claim: Options lose value as expiration approaches (time decay); theta increases near expiration
support: Time decay concept explained
mechanism: Option value = intrinsic + time value; time value decays non-linearly
validation: Compare model predictions to market prices

title: Swing trading holds 2-5 days
claim: Swing trading intermediate-term strategy; positions held 2-5 days capturing larger moves than scalping/day trading
support: Swing trading definition and time horizon
mechanism: Longer holding period captures larger swings; lower transaction costs than day trading
assumptions: Market volatility sufficient for swing size
validation: Measure average holding periods and move sizes

title: Swing trader discipline and risk
claim: Successful swing traders maintain discipline, defined risk per trade, position sizing rules, and emotional control
support: Trader characteristics described
mechanism: Discipline enforces rules; defined risk limits losses
validation: Audit trade logs vs documented trading rules

title: Swing trading market preferences
claim: Swing traders prefer stocks with high volume and volatility in established uptrends or downtrends
support: Market selection criteria described
mechanism: Liquidity ensures entry/exit; volatility creates swings; trends provide direction bias
validation: Backtest market selection criteria; measure performance correlation

title: Swing trading analysis methods
claim: Swing traders combine fundamental analysis (earnings, sector trends) with technical analysis (support/resistance, patterns)
support: Both analysis types presented as valid
mechanism: Fundamentals provide direction bias; technicals provide entry/exit timing
validation: Test predictive power separately and combined

title: Swing trading psychology resilience
claim: Swing traders must manage drawdowns psychologically; can't overtrade in drawdowns; must follow plan during losses
support: Psychology described as critical
mechanism: Losses trigger revenge trading; discipline prevents emotional decisions
validation: Compare trading frequency/size vs plan during drawdowns

title: Position sizing prevents catastrophic loss
claim: Swing traders use position sizing (risk 1-2% per trade) and money management rules to survive drawdowns
support: Position sizing and money management described as essential
mechanism: Fixed risk per trade prevents account ruin; drawdown manageable with small position sizes
validation: Check historical trades for position sizing adherence
